🔥🇲🇽 <u>The Old INE Runs the New Right-Wing Party</u>

A Contralínea investigation by Nancy Flores maps how Somos, the party built out of Claudio X. González's "Marea Rosa," is staffed by the people who ran Mexico's electoral institute. Former INE president Lorenzo Córdova, who wants to be the right's presidential candidate in 2030, is a member. So are ex-councillors Leonardo Valdés Zurita, Marco Antonio Baños and Rodrigo Morales, and more than 10 former INE directors.

Edmundo Jacobo Molina was INE executive secretary for almost 15 years and controlled its structure, appointments and budget. He now runs the party's political training center. Contralínea reports that a group loyal to Jacobo and Córdova still holds senior posts inside the INE, including areas that handle the voter roll.

Somos's citizens' advisory council includes former Supreme Court justices Cossío, Ríos Farjat and Laynez, Fox's foreign minister Jorge Castañeda, and María Amparo Casar of Mexicanos Contra la Corrupción.

For years they sold themselves as neutral referees.
banner: INE VETERANS RUN RIGHT-WING PARTY SOMOS

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Demián Bichir: Amnesty Now for the 15 Million</u>

At the Morelia International Film Festival, Mexican actor Demián Bichir said the only way to end the migration crisis in the United States is an amnesty and real immigration reform for the roughly 15 million undocumented people who keep the US economy running. They need a clean slate, he said.

He knows how that works. Bichir said he is himself a product of the last amnesty, signed 40 years ago by a Republican, Ronald Reagan.

In Morelia he presented Mujer Santuario, a documentary he produced about a woman hiding from deportation inside a church. He said both big US parties use migrants as "cannon fodder," especially when elections come around.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico Delivers Its Rio Grande Water to the US, Drought and All</u>

Mexico has met its minimum annual delivery of Rio Grande water to the United States under the 1944 Water Treaty, the Foreign Ministry (SRE) reported on October 24, the day the first year of delivery cycle 37 closed. Under the plan both countries agreed on February 3, 2026, that minimum is about 431.7 million cubic meters a year.

The water went north during an extreme drought in the border region. The SRE says it was done without putting at risk the water people drink or the crops they grow, and that human consumption and essential farming stay the priority.

Last year Washington was threatening tariffs over this water. This year Mexico delivered it.
banner: WATER TREATY: MEXICO DELIVERS IN DROUGHT

🇲🇽🎨 "All students must have a scholarship, because they need it, because we want all of them to study." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Colima, Colima Some argue scholarships should only go to students averaging 9 or 10. She said that when she was Mexico City's head of government such a scholarship existed, and instead of motivating students it split classrooms into "good students and bad students, those who have a scholarship and those who don't." With the universal Benito Juárez scholarship for high school and Rita Cetina for secondary school, about 400,000 more young people reached high school this year. "Education is the best thing we can give our children. First comes love, and second a good education."
